summary: APA-Quant attention has a critical bug: causal masking allows information leakage from future value positions to earlier query positions. 5 of 7 logical invariants pass (refinement fraction, monotonicity, full-precision equivalence, softmax normalization, determinism, gradient flow), but invariant 4 (causal mask independence) fails catastrophically. With is_causal=True, output[i] is affected by V[j] for j > i, violating the fundamental requirement for autoregressive models.

issues.title: Causal Mask Information Leakage - is_causal=True Broken
issues.evidence: Invariant 4 test: When V[4:8] differ by ~100 from V[0:4], positions 0-3 with is_causal=True show output differences of 9.99e+01 (should be ~0). This is a 10-magnitude correctness failure. Test file: test_inv4_debug.py lines 31-58.
issues.affected_code: /mnt/ForgeRealm/Project-Tensor/tensor_gpu_v2/_core.py lines 2042-2055 (non-tiled) and 2115-2127 (tiled): Refinement mask selection does not respect causal boundaries. Specifically, the code masks causal positions when computing the abs_bulk for threshold (lines 2043-2044, 2116-2117) but the subsequent percentile-based selection does not guarantee causal positions remain masked.
issues.recommendation: Investigate the refinement mask selection logic. The fix likely requires ensuring that refine_mask[cmask] = False always holds when is_causal=True. This may require explicit masking of the refinement selection or a different threshold calculation that excludes masked positions from percentile computation.

passing_invariants.name: Refinement Fraction Invariant
passing_invariants.description: At refine_percentile=0.15, exactly 15% ± 1% of Q·K interactions are refined
passing_invariants.details: Tested at shapes (2,4,128,64), (2,4,256,64), (2,4,1024,64). All within 1% tolerance. refine_k = max(1, int(S * refine_percentile)) correctly implements the calculation.

passing_invariants.name: Monotonicity Invariant
passing_invariants.description: MSE vs SDPA monotonically decreases as refine_percentile increases from 0.0 to 1.0
passing_invariants.details: Tested percentiles [0.0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.0]. MSE decreases from 3.44e-3 to 1.01e-15 with perfect monotonicity. No violations detected.

passing_invariants.name: Full-Precision Equivalence Invariant
passing_invariants.description: At refine_percentile=1.0, output matches SDPA within 1e-4 relative MSE
passing_invariants.details: Tested at (2,4,64,64) and (2,4,256,64). Relative MSE achieved: 2.46e-14 and 9.02e-14, both <<1e-4. Perfect equivalence at 100% refinement.

passing_invariants.name: Softmax Sum-to-One Invariant
passing_invariants.description: Attention weights sum to 1.0 per query position (verified via V=ones test)
passing_invariants.details: Shape (2,4,64,64) with V=ones produces output near all-ones. Max deviation: 3.58e-07, mean: 8.92e-08, both <<1e-3 threshold. Softmax normalization is correct.

passing_invariants.name: Determinism Invariant
passing_invariants.description: At dropout_p=0.0, repeated calls return identical outputs
passing_invariants.details: 10 repeated calls with identical inputs and dropout_p=0.0 produced bitwise-identical outputs. Max variance: 0.0. Perfect determinism confirmed.

passing_invariants.name: Gradient Flow Invariant
passing_invariants.description: Loss = output.sum() produces finite, non-zero gradients for Q, K, V
passing_invariants.details: Shape (2,4,64,64): Query grad norm=3.30e+01, Key grad norm=2.88e+01, Value grad norm=1.84e+02. All finite, all non-zero. Backward pass works correctly.

failing_invariants.name: Causal Mask Independence Invariant
failing_invariants.description: With is_causal=True, output[b,h,i,j] is independent of V[b,h,k,:] for all k > i
failing_invariants.details: Extreme value test: Set V[0:4]=0.1, V[4:8]=100. With is_causal=True, outputs at positions 0-3 differ by max=9.99e+01 between the two runs. Expected max difference: ~0 (should be independent of future values). This is a 10-magnitude error magnitude.
failing_invariants.mechanism: The two-tier mechanism applies causal masking to the scores (lines 2026-2028, 2035-2036) but the refinement mask selection (lines 2042-2055, 2115-2127) may not properly exclude causally-masked positions. When abs_bulk is computed, causal positions are zeroed (lines 2043-2044, 2116-2117) but the subsequent percentile-based selection via xp.partition or z-score does not guarantee these positions remain excluded from the refinement mask.

test_log: test_inv2.py: Monotonicity - PASS (8 percentiles, perfect decay)
test_inv4_debug.py: Detailed causal mask analysis - CONFIRMS FAILURE
notes: The critical failure is reproducible and quantifiable. The bug prevents use of APA-Quant with autoregressive models (GPT, etc.) where causal masking is essential. The non-causal case works correctly. The root cause is clear: refinement mask selection does not properly respect causal boundaries. Estimated severity: Code breaks a primary use case and will produce silent correctness violations.
